newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pharmacia and Upjohn to close 24 of 57 plants - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia and Upjohn to close 24 of 57 plants - paper.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn intends to close down 24 of 57 plants, Swedish daily Finanstidningen said on Wednesday.
The closures are part of a five-point programme of measures to increase profitability and cut costs, the newspaper said.
"We have a bit too much of everything," acting chief executive Jan Ekberg was quoted as saying.
Ekberg could not yet say which plants or how many of the company's 31,700 employees would be affected by the restructuring.

He declined to disclose how much the programme would cost initially or how much savings would be generated, saying more detailed information about the company's plans would be released at the end of this quarter.
"It (savings) will show eventually," Ekberg was quoted as saying. "The aim is to compare ourselves with other pharmaceutical companies."
He said the group underestimated the problems of merging two companies, Pharmacia of Sweden and Upjohn of the United States, in 1995.
"We must get a company with a common view," he told Finanstidningen.
The group has had problems with profitability and has issued a couple of profit warnings which have sent its shares tumbling on the New York and Stockholm stock exchanges.

It latest warning came less than a week before it was due to release first quarter earnings. In the first three months of the year, its sales dropped 6.1 percent to $1.64 billion while earnings per share fell to $0.37 from $0.44.
The Swedish shareholders associations found the programme vague.

"If they haven't realised these things out until now they should think again, they are pretty basic measures that can be taken out of any textbook about mergers," Lars Milberg of the association was quoted as saying.
